column3: NASB renders “sounding brass” as “a noisy gong.”
NASB adds “the gift of” and renders “understand” as “know.”
NASB reads “to be burned,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “that I may boast.” It adds “to feed the poor” and renders “I am profited nothing” as “it profits me nothing.”
NASB restructures the verse; “envious” is rendered “jealous,” “boastful” is “brag,” and “puffed up” is “arrogant.”
NASB renders “easily provoked” as “provoked” and “keeps account of wrongs” as “take into account a wrong suffered.”
NASB renders “delights at” as “rejoice in” and “in the truth” as “with the truth.”
NASB follows the critical text (“fails”); it adds “gifts of” and “there are,” and renders “be abated” as “be done away.”
NASB follows the critical text without “then”; “the in part” is rendered “the partial.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “I was speaking” as “I used to speak” and “the things of the child” as “childish things.”
NASB renders “glass” as “mirror” and “in obscurity” as “dimly.”
